sources.title: Human History Map: Thai Kingdoms imported index and geometry
sources.note: Local index and world-600/world-700 decoded; metadata only. Polygon contains Kunming, Dien Bien and Luang Prabang diagnostic points, excludes Dali, Hanoi and Chiang Mai. Not reconstructed ethnic borders.

sources.title: Pittayawat Pittayaporn, Layers of Chinese Loanwords in Proto-Southwestern Tai (2014)
sources.note: Manusya 17(3), pp.47 to68. Original publisher abstract directly read through indexed DOI page: four layers and proposed eighth-to-tenth-century dispersal. Full PDF unavailable; no individual loanword claims taken from inaccessible tables.

sources.title: Pittayawat Pittayaporn, The Phonology of Proto-Tai (Cornell, 2009)
sources.note: Original indexed dissertation abstract and printed p.110, Table3-26 checked. Comparative reconstruction, not surviving ancient speech recording or manuscript.

sources.title: Laurent Sagart, How Many Independent Rice Vocabularies in Asia? (2011)
sources.note: Direct full text, Austronesian and Tai-Kadai section. Uses paddy-field and dehusked-rice reconstructions, and proposes Tai-to-Chinese borrowing. Wider macrofamily hypothesis is contested and not presented as fact.

sources.title: Christopher D. Buckley and colleagues, Kra-Dai languages and weaving technologies (2025)
sources.note: Full paper read: pp.2 to5, Figure1, and p.20 loom word. Proto-Tai weave reconstruction is indirect evidence; contemporary family transmission and ceremonial skirt are explicitly later comparisons, not dated600to800.

sources.title: Tateishi Kenji, The Acceptance of Han Culture during the Tang to Wu Zhou Period in Yunnan (2021)
sources.note: Tokai University, pp.75 to91, DOI10.18995/24344710.6.75. Full PDF read. Heading 大周故河東州刺史之碑 and Japanese translation. English abstract mistakenly says Annan/Dongzhou and gives February3,698; Japanese body consistently Anning/Hedong and November14,698. Public uses year698 only. Death-year conversion in body also inconsistent; excluded. No Tai attribution established.

sources.title: Academia Sinica, The historical debate over Dai and Tai kingdoms
sources.note: Direct academic project page, final Academic Debate concerning Nanzhao section only. It rejects Dai/Tai ruling-family identification and notes Bai/Yi discussion. Earlier sections contain legendary and anachronistic Lanna chronology; none used.

sources.title: Chris Baker and Pasuk Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand, second edition (2009)
sources.note: Direct publisher/distributor preview, printed pp.4 to8. Valley cultivation and mueang model are broad historical synthesis, not specifically attested600to800 institutions. Thai written evidence thirteenth century. Later city-state comparison explicitly labeled.

batchIdentityNotes.note: Exact ID only; no sharing. Imported name Thai Kingdoms is not support for centralized rule600to800. Two identical features600to700/700to800, bbox100.1224,19.4785,106.4297,26.0563. Anning material is Tang/Wu Zhou-associated and NOT ethnically assigned as Tai. Sukhothai, kingdom-of-sukhotai, Ayutthaya, lan-na, Thailand, Dvaravati, Nanzhao and earlier Thai culture records remain separate. Parent explicitly approved cautious regional-context approach following identity alert. No fabricated ancient Thai script or later institutions projected backwards.
